title: Debrecen spot data show that the 1981 sunspot-number fall at matched F10.7 and Mg II is a fall in group count, while spot count, spot area and small-spot share do not fall (1978-1983)
abstract: Question: near January 1981, the international sunspot number (SN) fell by about 13% relative to F10.7 and Mg II. Did fewer spots, smaller spots, or fewer groups cause the fall? Method: we used the Debrecen Photoheliographic Data (DPD), which gives the position and area of each spot. In 1978-1983 most DPD days come from Gyula plates, which are not part of the SN network. We counted DPD groups, spots, spot area and spot-size classes. We also joined spots into clusters by a fixed distance rule (2.5-10 degrees), without any observer grouping. We fitted quasi-Poisson models of daily counts against F10.7 or Mg II, with DPD source effects, for November 1978 to June 1983 and for the same cycle phase in Cycles 22-24. Intervals come from a paired residual block bootstrap. Results: across January 1981, at matched F10.7, SN changes by 0.873 (95% interval 0.83-0.92) and DPD groups by 0.884 (0.84-0.93). The ratio SN/DPD groups is 0.973-1.035 in all twelve model variants. Position clusters at 6 and 10 degrees fall by 0.876 and 0.841, but 2.5-degree clusters do not change (1.015). DPD spot count (1.014, 0.89-1.16), spot area (1.060) and the share of spots of 2 millionths of the hemisphere or less (0.993) do not fall with flat levels. Area per group increases by about 20%. With separate time slopes, DPD spot counts also fall by 15%. DPD groups and 6-degree clusters also fall at the same phase in Cycles 22 and 23 (0.94 and 0.89; 0.87 and 0.91). Conclusion: under the main model, the same spots and spot area occur in about 12% fewer groups. The Wolf formula gives each group a weight of 10, so this concentration lowers SN at the same emission. We find no small-spot deficit. Limitations: DPD 1979-1984 is preliminary, the spot-count result depends on the time model, only four cycle windows exist, and DPD source and method changes prevent cross-cycle level tests. External data stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Post/pre factors across January 1981 (November 1978 to June 1983) at matched emission, with 95% block-bootstrap intervals, for three model variants. SN, the Locarno counts, DPD groups and DPD position clusters at 6 and 10 degrees fall by 12-16%. DPD spot counts, the smallest-spot class and spot area do not fall with flat levels. SN divided by DPD groups stays near 1.

The same cycle-phase window (cycle months 32-87, split at month 58) in Cycles 21-24, at matched F10.7. DPD groups and 6-degree clusters also fall in Cycles 22 and 23. SN falls more in Cycle 21 and Cycle 24 than in Cycles 22 and 23.

Quarterly observed/predicted ratios, November 1978 to June 1983, from a display power law in F10.7 fitted before 1981. Left: SN, DPD groups and 6-degree clusters fall together after 1980. Right: DPD spots and spot area do not follow the SN fall.
